description: One SEO defect fixed per iteration, 15 iterations. Work too large for a single iteration is recorded here with grounded evidence so the next iteration can pick it up without re-auditing. Note: the repo root PRD.json belongs to a separate enterprise-readiness initiative and must not be edited by this loop.

stories.title: Fix meta-tag manager: repeated tags, stale tags, clobbered viewport
stories.evidence: src/components/SEO.tsx wrote article:tag through updateMetaTag in a forEach, which reuses the first matching element, so an article with 5 tags shipped 1. Article and citation meta survived navigation to non-article routes. The effect rewrote name=viewport on every route, dropping viewport-fit=cover from index.html:5. The tags prop was in the effect dependency array by array identity, rerunning the whole DOM write on every render.
stories.resolution: Added setMetaTagList for repeatable tags, removeMetaTags (querySelectorAll, not querySelector), an ARTICLE_META_TAGS clear list, unconditional clearing of citation_publication_date/citation_source/abstract, removal of the viewport write, and a content-keyed memo for tags. Covered by src/components/__tests__/SEO.test.tsx (5 tests).

stories.title: Replace the stale static sitemap with a generated one
stories.evidence: public/sitemap.xml holds 9 URLs with lastmod values from 2025-07-15 to 2025-07-24 and no articles. robots.txt points crawlers at https://danpearson.net/sitemap.xml and public/_redirects:10 maps that path to the static file with a 200, so the SitemapXML.tsx route never serves. Every article published since July 2025 is absent from the sitemap Google reads.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide between a build-time generator writing public/sitemap.xml and routing /sitemap.xml to the app; only one source of truth remains
Generated sitemap includes homepage, main pages, every published article, and the topic/tag/author/category archives
lastmod reflects each article's updated_at, not the build date
robots.txt Sitemap line matches the served URL
Static and dynamic sitemaps cannot disagree - the losing one is deleted
stories.notes: Likely spans more than one iteration: the generator needs Supabase access at build time or a scheduled edge function. If so, split into SEO-002a (generator) and SEO-002b (wire-up + robots).

stories.title: Add SEO meta to the four indexable pages that ship none
stories.evidence: src/pages/CookiePolicy.tsx, PrivacyPolicy.tsx, TermsOfService.tsx and DateArchive.tsx render no <SEO> component, so each inherits whatever meta the previously viewed route left in the head. RSSFeed.tsx, RobotsTxt.tsx and SitemapXML.tsx also lack it but serve non-HTML and are correctly excluded.
acceptanceCriteria: Each of the four pages renders <SEO> with a title, description and canonical URL specific to that page
DateArchive builds its title and description from the year/month route params
Legal pages are indexable; thin or duplicate date archives use noIndex where appropriate

stories.title: Audit robots.txt Disallow rules for false positives
stories.evidence: public/robots.txt disallows /2023/ and /2025/. If DateArchive or any legacy article URL lives under a year path, live content is being blocked from indexing. Needs confirmation against App.tsx routes and published article slugs before changing anything.
acceptanceCriteria: Every Disallow rule is matched against the real route table in src/App.tsx
Rules that block indexable content are removed or narrowed
Rules that block genuinely thin pages stay, with a comment saying which route they cover

stories.title: Scope the Google Scholar citation_* meta to article pages
stories.evidence: src/components/SEO.tsx writes citation_title, citation_author and citation_site_title on every route including the homepage and the contact page. These are Highwire Press tags for scholarly articles; emitting them site-wide is noise at best.
acceptanceCriteria: citation_* tags are emitted only when type === 'article'
They are cleared on non-article routes

stories.title: Audit StructuredData output against Google's Rich Results requirements
stories.evidence: src/components/SEO/StructuredData.tsx is 590 lines covering 14 schema types. Not yet validated - required properties, @id linking between Person/Organization/Article, and duplicate JSON-LD blocks across nested SEO usages are all unverified.
acceptanceCriteria: Each emitted schema type is checked against its required-property list
Only one JSON-LD script per schema type per page
Article schema links author and publisher by @id rather than repeating them inline
stories.notes: Too large for one iteration. Split per schema family: article/person/organization first, then faq/howto/product, then the rest.
